disputes.reason: This 5301-byte function was folded into the 'networking' label solely because it sits inside the 0x4b5d70-0x4bab50 address run alongside the GameSpy server-browser calls (0x616f80-0x617c10, hostname/mapname/gametype/numplayers key parsing). But its own decompiled body makes zero GameSpy/socket/mutex calls -- it only calls FUN_4b8a60 (a wide-string list-append helper shared across the file), a small formatter FUN_4b8d30, and UI widget-list functions FUN_5764a0/576890/576990/576a20, then builds display strings via swprintf/wcscat from tag-lookup keys such as 'ui\shell\main_menu\multiplayer_type_select\join_game\join_game_rules_strings', 'oddball_edit\var_speed_with_ball', 'race_edit\var_race_type', 'vehicle_options_edit\var_vehicle_set', etc. -- i.e. it formats the oddball/race/teamplay/vehicle/item game-variant rules into a wide string for display, with no network I/O at all. modules.json independently carries a pre-existing, higher-quality identification for this exact address (source 'big20', not derived from this slice run) naming it game_variant_build_rules_description and classifying it 'interface' (0.6) -- 'Formats the multiplayer game-variant rules summary ... into a wide-char string from ui\shell string-list tags, for the jo[in game screen]'. The slice's own cea-string-hint also lists a directly relevant hit, server_list_menu_update (interface), among its matches. All three independent signals (own decompiled body, prior big20 name recovery, cea-string-hint) point to 'interface', not 'networking'; only the address's location inside the wider server-browser run supports 'networking', and that run-based signal is exactly what this function's own body contradicts. The rest of the 0x4b5d70-0x4bab50 run (password/hostname/mapname/gametype key parsing, WaitForSingleObject/ReleaseMutex around 0x616f80-0x617c10 GameSpy calls, qsort of server list) is still solidly 'networking' -- this is a single-function outlier, not a call to relabel the whole run.

Decompiled body (confirmed via pack.py) is a plain two-field {uint,uint} struct comparator with no strings/globals/callees -- classic qsort comparator shape, but nothing in it is network-specific. It sits only 8 bytes after the last confirmed networking/server-browser function (0x4baae0, end of the GameSpy server-list code) and only 48 bytes before 0x4baba0, the first function of the video-settings run (seeded by the '-vidmode' string). The video-settings run's 0x4bad40 (run-labelled interface) calls FUN_4baba0 (which enumerates display resolutions per its cea/context) and then _qsort, with no other comparator candidate anywhere in that run; a {field0,field1}-tie-break compare matches a resolution list (width, then height) far better than anything in the server-browser code, which already has its own qsort comparator for the server list (0x4ba9c0 -> 0x4baa60, which references the 'numplayers' string, is a completely different, string-driven comparator). This looks like a one-function run-boundary slip: 0x4bab50 is almost certainly the resolution-list qsort comparator called from the following interface/video-settings run (0x4baba0-0x4bb640), not a member of the preceding networking run.

notes: Reviewed all 300 assignments in out/phase1/assign_06.json against out/slices/06.md, modules.json, and 9 pack.py decompiles (0x4c6340, 0x4ba270, 0x4b8da0, 0x4bab50, 0x4c9770, and spot checks of the items/math runs' anchor functions). Overall the slice is careful and well-reasoned: it correctly caught two stale 0.8-confidence Ghidra-name seeds that were actually mismatched symbols -- 0x4c6340 ('weapon_get_first_person_animation_time', confirmed via decompile to be plain argv '-console' flag parsing) and 0x4c7f10 ('weapon_stop_reload', confirmed to be the main loop driving checkpoint/timedemo with MsgWaitForMultipleObjects) -- and reassigned both to 'main' with body-level justification. The huge items run (0x4bbb50-0x4c62f0) is well anchored by cea-pdb hits for item_update/item_accelerate ('ground point'), projectile_detonate ('gravity'), and trigger_create_projectiles ('primary trigger'/'secondary trigger'); the repeated per-type triads calling FUN_4e9c20/4e9cd0/4ec590/4ec670/4ec940/4f05e0/4f52c0/4f54b0/4f6ec0 are consistent with item-subtype (weapon/projectile/equipment/garbage) callback boilerplate and don't need to be split into 'objects'. The math tail (0x4ca4b0-0x4cda90) and its gating from math_initialize (0x4cd3f0, '-noSSE') check out, including the matrix4x3_* seeds (0.85 confidence) which are self-consistent with their neighbors. The 'main' run (0x4c6340-0x4ca1a0) is strongly corroborated by repeated cea-string-hint 'main' hits across several of its members (0x4c6390, 0x4c6f30, 0x4c7610 main(4), 0x4c9a70, 0x4ca1a0) despite also containing menu-loading calls (load_ui_map/load_main_menu/load_ui_widget), so keeping that as one file/module rather than splitting into 'shell' looks right. I checked a handful of weaker cea-string-hint mismatches (0x4b3450 hint ai(1), 0x4badc0 hint game(1), 0x4c0670/0x4c4c40 tied hints, 0x4c6f30 hint interface(2), 0x4c9260 hint interface(2), 0x4c9770 hint cache(3)/scenario(1)) and in every case the hint was a single/weak/generic-format-string match that was outweighed by direct seed signatures or tight call-chain context within the run, so none of those are raised as disputes. No unknown or lib:* entries are present in this slice, and I found no D3DX/CRT/GameSpy/Bink library code mislabelled as engine code or vice versa. The two disputes above are the only places I found where a function's own decompiled body contradicts the run-based module label it inherited from its neighbors.
